en: Theravāda Vinaya Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga Pācittiyakaṇḍa
The Chapter on Those Who Have Been Maidens.
75. The Training Rule on Being Fully Twelve Years Old.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, nuns who were twelve years of seniority but had not been authorized by the Saṅgha were giving the full admission.
They were foolish and incompetent;
they did not know what was allowable or what was unallowable.
The co-residents were also foolish and incompetent;
they did not know what was allowable or what was unallowable.
Those bhikkhunīs who were of few desires... [as before] ...were indignant, complained, and grumbled:
“How indeed can nuns who have completed twelve years of seniority ordain others without being authorized by the Saṅgha?
… [The Buddha asked: “Is it true, monks, that nuns who have completed twelve years of seniority are ordaining others without being authorized by the Saṅgha?
“It is true, Blessed One.”
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them:
“… How indeed, monks, can nuns who have completed twelve years of seniority ordain others without being authorized by the Saṅgha?
This, monks, is neither for the inspiration of those without faith nor for the increase of those with faith…” [and so on].
Having rebuked them … and having given a discourse on the Dhamma, he addressed the bhikkhus:
“I allow you, bhikkhus, to grant formal authorization for a bhikkhunī who has completed twelve years [of seniority] to give the full admission.”
And furthermore, monks, it should be given in this way:
That nun who has completed twelve years of seniority should approach the Saṅgha, arrange her upper robe over one shoulder,
pay homage at the feet of the elder nuns, sit down on her haunches, raise her joined palms, and speak as follows:
‘Venerable ladies, I, the bhikkhunī named so-and-so, who am twelve years of age and have fulfilled the requirements, request formal authorization from the Saṅgha to give the full admission.
She should request a second time;
she should request a third time.
That bhikkhunī should be examined by the Saṅgha: “Is this bhikkhunī competent and modest?
If she is both foolish and shameless, it should not be granted.
If she is foolish but modest, it should not be granted.
If she is competent but lacks a sense of shame, it should not be given.
If she is both competent and possesses a sense of shame, it should be given.
And furthermore, monks, it should be given in this way.
The Saṅgha should be informed by a competent and experienced bhikkhunī:
“Let the noble Saṅgha hear me.
This bhikkhunī named so-and-so, who is twelve years of standing, requests from the Saṅgha permission to give the full admission.”
If it seems appropriate to the Saṅgha, let the Saṅgha grant formal authorization for the nun named so-and-so, who has completed twelve years [of seniority], to give the full admission.
This is the motion.
Let the noble ladies of the Saṅgha listen to me.
This nun, [name], who has completed twelve years [of seniority], requests the Sangha for authorization to give the higher ordination.
The Sangha grants authorization to this nun, [name], who has completed twelve years [of seniority], to give the higher ordination.
Whichever noble lady approves of granting authorization to this nun, [name], who has completed twelve years [of seniority], to give the higher ordination, let her be silent.
"Whoever does not approve of this, let her speak.
The Sangha has granted permission for the nun named so-and-so, who is full twelve years of age, to give the higher ordination.
Since the Sangha approves and is therefore silent, I shall so hold it."
Then the Blessed One, having rebuked those bhikkhunīs in many ways for being difficult to support...
[and so forth] ...said this: "And thus, bhikkhus, should the bhikkhunīs recite this training rule:
'If any bhikkhunī who has completed twelve years of seniority, not authorized by the Saṅgha, should give the full admission, it is an offense entailing expiation.'"
"But whichever" means whichever such... "nun" means...
[as before]... nun.
...pe... in this context, "bhikkhunī" refers to one who is intended in this sense.
"One who has completed twelve years" means one who has reached the age of twelve.
"Unappointed" means that the authorization for giving the full admission has not been granted by means of a formal act consisting of a motion and a second.
"Should give the full admission" means...
If she should ordain [a woman], or if,
thinking "I will give the full admission," she seeks out a group, a preceptor, an alms bowl, or a robe, or if she demarcates a boundary, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
With the motion (ñatti), there is an offense of wrong-doing.
With two formal proclamations, there are offenses of wrong-doing (*dukkaṭa*).
At the conclusion of the formal proclamation, it is an offense of expiation (*pācittiya*) for the preceptor;
it is an offense of wrong-doing for the assembly and for the teacher.
If it is a legitimate legal act and she perceives it as such, yet she ordains [a person], there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
If it is a legitimate legal act but she is uncertain of it, yet she ordains [a person], there is an offense of expiation.
If it is a legitimate legal act but she perceives it as an illegitimate legal act, yet she ordains [a person], there is an offense of expiation.
If it is an illegitimate legal procedure and one perceives it as a legitimate legal procedure, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
If it is an illegitimate legal procedure and one is uncertain of it, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
If it is an illegitimate legal procedure and one perceives it as an illegitimate legal procedure, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
There is no offense if she ordains one who has completed twelve years and is authorized by the Saṅgha;
or if she is insane.
"Regarding the first offender":
thus ends the fifth training rule.
